description: Sabotages for windows-namespace-request-sys's allocation-failure paths (NR-3): an allocation that fails is an error the caller receives, never a panic or an abort. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format.
notCoveredHere: The allocation-failure paths (NR-3) and the device-control helper with its entries through NR-2.5 (and the generic property query, NR-2.7) have entries. NR-2.5's own blind spot is the one the machine imposes: no entry of a dependency query was ever observed, because attaching a virtual disk needs an elevated token, so its entries and names are pinned against replies built from the structure's declared layout and a fake device, and a real entry's layout, where its names lie, and what a buffer too small for its entries returns are not covered. The catalogue's other entries, the capture of handles and paths, and the security descriptor's own parsing are not covered. SecurityDescriptor::try_clone's failure is a declared blind spot (see its survives entry): AlignedBuf::try_clone allocates exactly the size of a buffer that already exists, so no test can make it fail. The device-control helper's pending path is run through its seam, `overlapped_call`, with an overlapped ReadFile on a named pipe, because no file-system control pends on demand (an overlapped control pended in 0 of 20000 isolated runs). So the wait, the result read and the failure after pending are pinned with a call that is not a control; the one call that makes it a control, the DeviceIoControl argument list, is pinned by the controls themselves, and FSCTL_REQUEST_OPLOCK, which takes input and pends until another handle writes, reaches DeviceIoControl through the pending path as well (NR-2.2). The abort when the wait fails is not reachable: the event is the helper's own. The failures of the two descriptor allocations, in capture and in conversion, are reached through their shared function, `allocate`, which the tests call with a length no machine has; the OS names the real length, so no descriptor can be made to ask for it.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a capacity the machine cannot supply is reported under another code
sabotages.why: A query whose buffer cannot be allocated reports ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, the code a caller reads as 'ask for less'. Any other code would read as the call's own failure.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor allocation failure is reported as an invalid copy
sabotages.why: An allocation failure is its own failure, SecurityCaptureFailure::Allocate: an invalid copy would send a caller looking for a malformed descriptor.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor allocation failure carries the wrong code
sabotages.why: The error's raw code is ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, which a caller who funnels everything through raw_os_error reads as 'out of memory'.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a copy of security attributes drops the descriptor
sabotages.why: A copy that kept the inheritance choice but not the descriptor would open files with different security than the original.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a failed security copy is reported as a failed duplication
sabotages.why: A request's try_clone reports a failed copy of its security attributes as HandleCaptureFailure::CopySecurity, not as DuplicateHandle, which would send a caller looking at a handle that was never the problem.

sabotages.name: NR-3: an open request's copy forgets its security attributes
sabotages.why: The copy must open with what the original would; the attributes went through Clone before, and nothing but this test would notice a copy that dropped them.

sabotages.name: NR-3: an open-by-identifier request's copy forgets its security attributes
sabotages.why: As for the path-named open: the copy must carry the attributes the original does.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a descriptor alignment that is not a power of two is refused by the build
sabotages.why: AlignedBuf refuses such an alignment and `allocate` reports every refusal as an allocation failure, so a bad constant would read as out of memory on every call. The constant is asserted where it is defined.

sabotages.name: NR-3: a batch alignment that is not a power of two is refused by the build
sabotages.why: As for the descriptor's: `perform` reports every refusal of the allocation as ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, so a bad constant would be misreported as out of memory.

sabotages.name: NR-3: BLIND SPOT: a failed copy of a descriptor is reported as an invalid copy
sabotages.why: Declared blind spot, not a control. SecurityDescriptor::try_clone allocates exactly the size of a buffer that already exists, so no test can make it fail; the failure it would report is the shared `allocation()`, whose result the other entries pin.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: the event handed to an overlapped control does not suppress the completion packet
sabotages.why: A handle on a completion port gets a packet when an overlapped call completes unless the event's low bit is set. Without it a control would reach a consumer's loop as a completion it never asked for.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a control is told its output buffer is empty
sabotages.why: The buffer length the device is given is the buffer's own; a shorter one makes every control fail for want of room.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a control that completed reports no bytes written
sabotages.why: The byte count is what a caller checks the reply's size by; a count of nothing would read as an empty reply.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a reply larger than the structure is read as the node
sabotages.why: A reply of any size but the structure's is reported and not read, because a value taken from a buffer the device did not fill would read as a node.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a reply smaller than the structure is read as the node
sabotages.why: The other half of the size check: a short reply leaves the buffer's remainder as it was, and reading it would report a node the device never named.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: the node is read from the first byte alone
sabotages.why: The node is a whole ULONG, carried unaltered; a value above 255 would be truncated.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a call still running is not waited for
sabotages.why: A call that reports ERROR_IO_PENDING is waited for and its result read; without that the caller is handed the pending code while the device is still writing into a buffer about to be freed.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: the wait for a call still running does not wait
sabotages.why: The result is read without waiting, so a call that has not completed is reported as ERROR_IO_INCOMPLETE and the device is left writing.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a call that completed after pending reports no bytes written
sabotages.why: The count a call that completed asynchronously wrote is read from GetOverlappedResult, and it is what a caller checks a reply's size by.

sabotages.name: NR-2.1: a call that failed after pending is reported as a success
sabotages.why: A call that pends and then fails reports its own code through GetOverlappedResult; discarding it would report success with whatever count was left.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: a control's input is not passed to the device
sabotages.why: An oplock request is refused without its input structure, so a helper that drops the input fails the control that takes one; none of the no-input controls could tell.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: the disk-extents entry sends a different control code
sabotages.why: The entry's whole meaning is the control code it sends; a neighbouring code is refused by a volume.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: a reply that needs more room is not asked again
sabotages.why: A volume with more extents than the first buffer holds is reported ERROR_MORE_DATA with a count; unless that code starts the retry, such a volume fails.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: the first answer may have room for no extent
sabotages.why: The device refuses a buffer with no room for one extent, so an entry that asks with none fails every volume.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: a count of nothing in a more-data reply allocates a buffer with no room for an extent
sabotages.why: A reply that says it needs more room and counts none must not shrink the next buffer below the one extent the device requires.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: the retry is not bounded by its constant
sabotages.why: The bound on attempts is the one the error reports; a loop that runs one more would spin a worker on a volume whose extents keep changing and report a number it did not use.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: a refusal by the device is retried as though it needed more room
sabotages.why: Any code but ERROR_MORE_DATA ends the attempts and is the device's own; retrying it would hide it behind an Unstable report.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: an answer that exactly fills what was written is refused
sabotages.why: A reply of exactly the size of the extents it counts is the normal case, so the size check refuses only a reply that is shorter.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: a call that says it wrote more than the buffer held is read
sabotages.why: A byte count beyond the buffer is the device's claim and not a fact; reading to it would slice outside the buffer.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: an extent's offset is read from its length
sabotages.why: Each extent is read field by field from where the device put it; a reader that takes the length for the start reports runs of disk that are not the volume's.

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: a negative length is accepted as zero
sabotages.why: A length below zero is not a length; reporting it as an empty run would hide a damaged answer behind a plausible one.
find:
length: u64::try_from(length)
                        .map_err(|_| malformed("an extent of negative length"))?,

sabotages.name: NR-2.2: a buffer the machine cannot supply is reported under another code
sabotages.why: The size is the device's to name, so a buffer for it may not be allocatable; that is ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, the code a caller reads as 'ask for less'. The function is shared by every entry that sizes a buffer from a reply.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the query names a different property
sabotages.why: The property id is what makes this the unique-id query and not another; the query structure is sent field by field and each field is checked where it lands.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the query asks a question other than the standard one
sabotages.why: A query type of 1 asks whether the property exists and returns no structure.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the entry asks for a different property than the one it names
sabotages.why: The unique-id entry's meaning is the property it queries; a neighbouring property's reply has a different layout and is not this one's.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the first buffer may be smaller than the header
sabotages.why: A buffer smaller than the header is refused as ERROR_BAD_LENGTH, so an entry that asks with less than the header fails on every disk.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a reply that needs more room is not asked again
sabotages.why: A buffer between the header and the reply is answered with ERROR_MORE_DATA and the header written; unless that code starts the retry, a reply larger than the first buffer fails.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the size is read from the version instead
sabotages.why: The reply's size is the second field of its header; read from the first, every reply is taken to be a few bytes long.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the retry is not bounded by its constant
sabotages.why: The bound on attempts is the one the error reports; a loop that runs one more would spin a worker on a reply whose size keeps changing and report a number it did not use.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a call that says it wrote more than the buffer held is read
sabotages.why: A byte count beyond the buffer is the device's claim and not a fact; reading to it would return bytes that were never written.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a reply shorter than its header is asked for again
sabotages.why: A call that wrote less than a header cannot have named a size; asking again at a size read from bytes it did not write would trust nothing.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a reply that exactly fills what was written is not accepted
sabotages.why: A reply whose size is exactly the bytes written is the normal case, and the one a buffer of the right size gets.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the reply is not cut to the size its header gives
sabotages.why: The first buffer is larger than most replies; its zero padding is not part of the reply, and a section found by its own size would otherwise be followed by bytes nobody wrote.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a header that is learned is not asked for again at the size it names
sabotages.why: A call that wrote only the header, or less than the reply, is asked again at the size the header names, and at exactly that size.
find:
// The header alone, or less than the reply: ask again at the size it names.
                capacity = size;
replace:
// The header alone, or less than the reply: ask again at the size it names.
                capacity = size - 1;

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a reply shorter than the size it names, in a buffer with room, is retried
sabotages.why: Asking again at a size the buffer already had would get the same buffer and the same answer; it is a malformed reply, and is reported as one.
find:
if size <= buffer.len() {
                    return Err(malformed("a reply shorter than the size it names"));
replace:
if size == 0 {
                    return Err(malformed("a reply shorter than the size it names"));

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a reply that needs more room but names a size already given is retried
sabotages.why: The same reasoning for the ERROR_MORE_DATA half: a size that was already given cannot be the answer to asking for more.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the device id descriptor's offset is read from the wrong field
sabotages.why: Each of the three offsets is read from its own field of the header; a reader that takes one from a neighbour reports one section's bytes as another's.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: an offset of zero is a section
sabotages.why: An offset of zero names no section; the measured disk reports only one of the three, and the other two must not be read from the header.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a section may start inside the header
sabotages.why: An offset inside the header would make the header its own section.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a section may say it is smaller than its own header
sabotages.why: A section is at least its own version and size; one that says less is not a section.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a section may run past the end of the reply
sabotages.why: A section whose own size is longer than the reply would be sliced past the bytes the device wrote.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a section's size is read from the wrong field
sabotages.why: A section's size is the second field of its own header; read from the first, its version is taken for its length.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the query type is written where the structure has the property
sabotages.why: The query type is a field of its own; written after the property id's offset it would overwrite the property.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: additional parameters are not written into the query
sabotages.why: A property that reads its additional parameters, as the unique-id property reads its first byte, would be asked without them.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the query is shorter than its structure when there are no additional parameters
sabotages.why: The device requires the structure in full; an input of only the fixed fields is ERROR_BAD_LENGTH.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a query for whether a property exists sends no input
sabotages.why: The exists query is a call with the query structure and no output; without the structure the device refuses it.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the generic query names a different property than the one configured
sabotages.why: The generic entry sends the property it was given and no other.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the generic query always asks the standard question
sabotages.why: The query type is the caller's; one that is always standard cannot ask whether a property exists or for a mask.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the generic query drops its additional parameters
sabotages.why: The additional parameters are sent as given: the unique-id property gives a different answer for them, which is how arrival is shown.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a query for whether a property exists is asked for a structure
sabotages.why: An exists query returns no structure; asked for one it would be refused as having a reply shorter than its header.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a copy of a generic query forgets its query type
sabotages.why: A copy asks the same question as the original.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a copy of a generic query forgets its additional parameters
sabotages.why: A copy sends the same parameters as the original.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: a generic reply's size is read from the wrong field
sabotages.why: The version and the size are separate fields of the header and are reported separately.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the exists query type is the mask query
sabotages.why: The named query types are the three Windows defines, and are distinct.

sabotages.name: NR-2.4: the NUMA entry asks for a different property
sabotages.why: The entry's meaning is the property it queries; a neighbouring property's reply is not a NUMA descriptor.

sabotages.name: NR-2.4: the NUMA entry asks a question other than the standard one
sabotages.why: A query for whether the property exists returns no structure, so there would be no node to read.

sabotages.name: NR-2.4: the node is read from the size field
sabotages.why: The node is the third field of the descriptor; each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: NR-2.4: the version is read from the node field
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it, and reported separately.

sabotages.name: NR-2.4: the size is read from the version field
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it, and reported separately.

sabotages.name: NR-2.4: a node that is not a node of any machine is altered
sabotages.why: The node is carried as the device wrote it; no value is documented as meaning none, so none is invented or clamped.

sabotages.name: NR-2.3: the version is read from the size field
sabotages.why: The version and the size are separate fields of the header and are reported separately.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the version is not put in the buffer
sabotages.why: The version is an input: the call refuses a buffer whose version field is not 1 or 2, so a request that does not set it is refused on every machine.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a first size below the structure is not raised
sabotages.why: A buffer under the structure's own size is ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, so asking at a configured smaller size would fail where raising it succeeds.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a size no larger than the one given is asked for again
sabotages.why: A reply that needs more room and names the room it already had is not going to be answered by asking the same question again.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the buffer is regrown to a size other than the one named
sabotages.why: The size the call names is the size it was measured to need; asking for a different one is a guess.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: ERROR_MORE_DATA is not a reason to ask again
sabotages.why: Which of the two a buffer too small for the entries returns is unverified, so both are followed.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: only one attempt is made
sabotages.why: A reply that needs more room than the first buffer has is only answered by asking again.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a status is altered on its way out
sabotages.why: The code is carried as the call returned it; the virtdisk errors have values above 16 bits, and one truncated to 16 bits names a different error.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the real call is given a size of nothing
sabotages.why: The size is how much the call may write; the real calls are the only test of the argument list.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the real call is not given the flags
sabotages.why: The flags are which way the query looks; without them the host direction is never asked for.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: HOST_VOLUMES also sets the disk-handle bit
sabotages.why: Each flag is its own bit; a flag that also says the handle is a disk asks a different question.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a new request asks for version one
sabotages.why: Version two is the one with the names, which is what the request is for; the default is documented as two.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a clone forgets the configured first size
sabotages.why: A copy of a request is the same request.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a reply that used more than it was given is read
sabotages.why: The call says how many bytes it used; a number beyond the buffer is a reply that cannot be trusted, and slicing by it would read outside the buffer.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a version one reply is read with version two's entry size
sabotages.why: The entries of each version have their own size, and the second entry of a reply is found by it.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a count the reply cannot hold is accepted up front
sabotages.why: The count is checked against the bytes the call used before any entry is read, so the refusal names the count and not whichever entry was reached first.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the ancestor level is read from the provider flags
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the type flags are read from the provider flags
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the device id is read from the vendor field
sabotages.why: Each field is read from where the structure has it.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the vendor is read from one byte late
sabotages.why: The vendor GUID is the sixteen bytes at its own offset.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: the host volume is read from the dependent volume's pointer
sabotages.why: Each name is read from the pointer the structure has for it, and the four are distinct.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a version one reply is read for names
sabotages.why: Names exist only in version two; reading them from a version one entry reads the next entry's bytes as pointers.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a null name pointer is not none
sabotages.why: A null pointer is an absent name, not an address to refuse.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a name pointer at the end of the reply is taken as inside it
sabotages.why: A pointer at the first byte past the reply is outside it, and is refused for that and not for what reading there would find.

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a name with no room for its terminator is accepted
sabotages.why: A string that runs to the end of the bytes used has no terminator within them, and what follows is not the call's.
replace: let terminated = offset + units.len() * size_of::<u16>() <= reply.len();

sabotages.name: NR-2.5: a name ending exactly at the end of the reply is refused
sabotages.why: The boundary the previous entry is one past: a terminator in the last two bytes used is within them.
